title: A job closed: delivery hint, reward paid once, old terms converted
description: A campaign switched from the previous runtime carries an open quest with old-style reward terms; the switch converts them. The hero takes a second job on the loop, delivers the goods (the receipt hints that the job may be complete), the DM closes it and pays the reward once; the converted legacy reward is paid through the same tool. On dm-loop-v1 only (Stage 4 §2 follow-ups).

steps.say: I ask the carter by the gate whether anyone in town pays for honest work.

steps.title: Fetch the carter's lost ledger
steps.description: Bettany's ledger fell off the cart on the north road.

expect.label: the old reward terms are converted on the switch to the loop

steps.say: I take the carter's other job: twenty sacks of flour to the bakery before dusk.

expect.label: the job is a quest (not a thread)

steps.say: I hand the sacks over to Bettany and the ledger I found on the road.

expect.label: the receipt hinted that the job may be complete
the flour reward is paid once
the converted legacy reward is paid through the loop

steps.say: I ask Bettany to pay me again for the flour.

meet.note: The carter becomes a character; no job yet.

rounds.text: Bettany the carter leans on her wheel. "Honest work, aye. Lost my ledger on the north road, and there's flour wanting hauling. Pick one or both."

arguments.name: Bettany the carter
arguments.description: A carter who works the gate road; blunt, fair, overworked.

take.note: The second job is a quest with reward terms; the sacks exist in the hero's hands.

rounds.text: "Twenty sacks, five coins, every one dry." She spits in her palm.

arguments.title: Haul the flour sacks
arguments.description: Twenty sacks of flour to the bakery before dusk.

arguments.name: Bettany's ledger
arguments.description: Found in the ditch on the north road.

deliver.note: The transfer to the issuer carries the open-job hint; the DM closes both jobs and pays each reward exactly once through claim_reward.

rounds.text: Bettany counts the sacks twice and turns the ledger over in her hands.
"Dry, every one. And my ledger, by the saints." She pays without haggling.

again.note: A second claim is rejected by the server; the DM plays the refusal.

rounds.text: She climbs back onto her cart.
